comparison: Both strongly support claims C4-C5, C22-C28 from the authors' prior human HD study (Berg et al., 2024). OpenEval emphasizes these establish rationale for the current hypothesis, while peer reviewers treat them as foundational context without critique. High agreement (Jaccard 0.9).

Perfect agreement on claims C101-C105 regarding DARPP-32 loss and phenotype changes. Both evaluations support these findings as valid characterization of disease progression in the model (Jaccard 1.0).

Both address claims C121-C123 about lack of DARPP-32 rescue. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED (appropriate negative finding), while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting the weakness of lacking behavioral/survival data to assess functional significance. Divergent interpretations (Jaccard 1.0).

Strong agreement on claims C106-C112 regarding INK128 target engagement, BBB permeability, and mTOR inhibition. Both accept this as foundational evidence for the therapeutic intervention (Jaccard 0.875).

Both support claims C29, C140, C178-C179 about therapeutic implications of early autophagy stimulation. OpenEval emphasizes validation of the hypothesis, while peer reviewers note translational potential but acknowledge uncertainty due to lack of behavioral data (Jaccard 0.8).
Strong agreement on claims C113-C115 regarding INK128 reversing autophagy phenotypes and normalizing lysosome numbers. Both evaluations support these as key therapeutic findings (Jaccard 0.75).

Both support claims C35-C45 about the tfLC3 reporter system capabilities and advantages. OpenEval emphasizes methodological validation, while peer reviewers implicitly endorse the approach by praising the stage-dependent analysis it enabled (Jaccard 0.692).

Both support claims C7-C8, C74-C77 regarding mHTT colocalization with autophagy markers. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of quantification, while peer reviewers explicitly highlight this as a study strength (Jaccard 0.6).

Both support claims C78-C81 about mHTT localization in autophagic vacuoles. OpenEval emphasizes specificity analysis and IEM quantification, while peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the comprehensive characterization (Jaccard 0.4).

Both support claims C50-C59 regarding IB characterization. OpenEval focuses on IHC data quality and age-dependent progression, while peer reviewers accept these as part of the mHTT pathology characterization (Jaccard 0.571).

Both support claims C60-C63 about ultrastructural IB characterization. OpenEval emphasizes IEM data and comparisons to human HD, while peer reviewers accept these findings without specific critique (Jaccard 0.286).

Both support claims C9-C13, C128, C174-C176 characterizing ALP alterations. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive synthesis across experiments, while peer reviewers explicitly praise the detailed stage-dependent characterization as novel and informative (Jaccard 0.36).

Both strongly support claims C116-C120 regarding mHTT reduction following INK128 treatment. OpenEval emphasizes rigorous quantification, while peer reviewers highlight this as key evidence for mTOR inhibition reducing toxicity in HD models (Jaccard 0.357).

Both support claims C82-C88 about delayed autophagosome acidification and lysosome depletion. OpenEval focuses on hue angle analysis methodology, while peer reviewers accept these as part of the comprehensive ALP characterization (Jaccard 0.143).

Both support claims C89-C97 regarding western blotting evidence of autophagy alterations. OpenEval acknowledges limitations (high variability, differences from human HD), while peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the detailed ALP characterization (Jaccard 0.172).

Both support claims C98-C100 about lipofuscin accumulation. OpenEval emphasizes EM quantification and comparison to human HD, while peer reviewers accept these as part of the comprehensive stage-dependent analysis (Jaccard 0.12).

Both support claims C130-C138 synthesizing western blotting and imaging findings. OpenEval discusses methodological considerations, while peer reviewers accept the age-dependent progression characterization (Jaccard 0.133).

Both support claims C142-C152 about mechanistic interpretation of autophagy enhancement. OpenEval notes sound logic with appropriate caveats, while peer reviewers accept the beneficial effect of autophagy upregulation in a stage-specific manner (Jaccard 0.091).
